RADiCAL T10 Run BookLuAG · CERN PS T10 · Aug 2026

Overview

Runs

Module: 4 capillaries, 14×14 mm, 2×2 (4 TL · 5 TR / 6 BL · 7 BR). Digitizer: CAEN DT5742, 5 GS/s, 1024 samples. One MCP on TR0, duplicated into both DRS groups.

From run 15: SiPM bias +1 V — final. Run-15 MIPs are the reference calibration.

Per-run QC: macros/QCv2.C

Timing follows σ_t ≈ 406/√E ⊕ 171 ps (MCP + DRS reference included, unsubtracted); the 3 GeV point lands within 3% of the prediction and the DQ-selected 9 GeV point (212 ± 11 ps) within 3% as well. Response is linear above 3 GeV (~660 ADC-eq/GeV); the sub-linear low-energy behavior is expected for shower-max sampling. σ/E improves with energy (20.4% at 7 GeV) as the peak grows past the roughly constant position-smearing term — the intrinsic-resolution measurement still wants a tracker or a tighter momentum slit. Gains drifted ~25% over the day (temperature); all points use their own MIPs. XCET tag thresholds are set per energy on the coincidence plateau (100/100/100/50 ADC-eq) — the original common 150 cut clipped ~9% of electrons at 5 GeV and ~5× at 7 GeV.

Still wanted

11 GeV point (negative beam); time-dependent calibration to recover run 29’s 20k drift-period events; lead-converter control runs per high-E point; one muon stopper run; optionally a re-taken 1 GeV point in the low-material beam configuration.

Selection

the beam is mostly electrons at 1 GeV

XCET coincidence: 8,818 / 10,264 = 85.9% — the 1 GeV beam is ~87% electrons by composition, so the tag is nearly the whole beam. The scarce species here is the hadron (~1,400 events) — as planned, this run is electron-rich and hadron-poor.

The 1 GeV spot (multiple scattering, regular beam optics) is larger than the module, so the response peak and the miss ridge overlap — the peak fit is unreliable and the energy point carries a large systematic. Selection

the edge of hardware tagging

XCET coincidence: 347 / 20,000 = 1.74%. The negative beam at 7 GeV is ~2.3% electrons, so the marginal 0.21 bar tag is running at roughly ~60–75% efficiency — thin, but real, and exactly the in-situ training point the >7 GeV offline selection needs. The prompt/slow window keeps 88.2% of tagged electrons; the apparent hadron acceptance (50.7%) is inflated by untagged real electrons in the probe sample — the lead-converter control run will measure the true leakage.

Runs 28+29 — 9 GeV, and an overnight lesson

1

Channel integrity & identification

standard treatment — and the overnight environment shows

Zero gaps in both files; TR0 correlation 0.998; pairings verified; MCP threshold unchanged (133–137 mV). Overnight cooling is visible everywhere: HG baseline noise fell ~7× vs the afternoon runs (dark counts), and the SiPM gains moved with temperature through the night.

2

Selection

the tag at its floor

At 0.15 bar the XCETs deliver ~3 photoelectrons: the threshold scan shows no plateau, so the tag runs at its floor (40 ADC-eq): coincidence 4.86% with singles 5.5%/5.3% — strongly correlated, so mostly real electrons. In-situ: the −9 GeV beam is ≥5% electrons, again well above the composition table. Threshold-floor purity (~90–94%) is the price; the offline selection variables carry the rest.

3

Results — after data-quality selection

the drift, found and fenced off

Overnight stability investigation — what actually drifted?

The merged timing first read 548 ps, and the initial suspicion was “overnight temperature.” A proper time-series study (23 half-hour slices, eight monitors: timing width and center, pooled MIP MPV, dark noise, MCP amplitude, trigger rate, DC baselines, tag health) tells a sharper story:

1. The insulated enclosure held all night. The SiPM gain (pooled MIP MPV) is constant to ±1% for 8.5 hours — the box sits at thermal equilibrium from its own electronics self-heating. No overnight bias adjustment was needed or would have helped.

2. A sharp morning event (~09:00–11:00) broke the equilibrium. Gain +60%, dark noise ×2, LG baselines shifting 40 mV — while the MCP amplitude stayed flat to ±1%. Consistent with hall HVAC / morning activity reaching the box, not gradual night cooling. (The day-scale gain ladder across runs — MIPs 404 → 327 → 281 → 216 from afternoon to night — is the same box slowly relaxing to closed-lid equilibrium after daytime accesses.)

3. The intermittent timing volatility is not hardware drift. Systematically exonerated: the digitizer (TR0 copy-vs-copy = 102–115 ps in every slice, including the worst), the MCP branch (the MCP-free capillary pair broadens too), gain/noise/rate (flat), tag purity (flat), and any single channel (all four capillaries fluctuate semi-independently). It survives an on-module purity cut, so it is not estimator noise alone either. The remaining explanation: at 9 GeV each capillary sees its smallest light share of the scan, and sporadic near-threshold srCFD outliers drag the per-event 4-capillary mean; a robust per-event combination (median, or amplitude-weighted with outlier rejection) is the identified analysis fix — hardware is not implicated.

quantityvalue
electrons on module (DQ sample)522
ΣLG peak5782 ± 160 ADC-eq
σ/E31.9 ± 3.8% (sparse)
srCFD shower-time σ212 ± 11 ps — trend predicts 218
Verdict. The 9 GeV point stands (212 ± 11 ps, on the photostatistics curve) and the investigation redeems the hardware: the box is stable all night at fixed bias — do NOT chase gain with bias; per-run MIPs absorb the day-scale relaxation. For the 11 GeV overnight: end the run before ~08:30 or log the box temperature; and implement the robust per-event timing combination to tame the low-light outliers. Run 29’s morning-ramp events remain recoverable with a time-dependent gain calibration.

The LG↔HG pairing was measured from amplitude correlations and is not diagonal: 4↔13, 5↔12, 6↔15, 7↔14 (verified per run: r = 0.93–0.96). Because chs 16/17 carry the same MCP pulse (amplitude correlation 0.999), their time difference is a free measurement of the DRS4 inter-group jitter: σ = 104.5 ± 2.2 ps.

2

Selection & calibration

tag electrons, calibrate every SiPM with its own MIPs

Electron tag

XCET 40 ∧ XCET 43, amplitude > 150 ADC: 2,466 / 25,000 = 9.9%. The rejected 22,534 events are the hadron/muon sample — used below as the calibration source.

MIP calibration + clip recovery

Landau MPV per HG channel: 142.5 / 164.9 / 159.8 / 120.9 ADC (chs 12/13/14/15) — a 36% gain spread measured to 0.3%. Clipped HG pulses are never discarded: HG-vs-LG transfer lines (fit in LG < 400, slopes 2.58–3.17) infer the true amplitude, and the CFD runs on the intact rising edge.

Energy response — no peak, and why

42.9% of tagged electrons miss the module; the rest form a position-driven continuum ending at a sharp direct-hit edge: position 2757 ± 54, width/position 10.5 ± 1.6% (upper bound on resolution at full response). No amount of statistics creates a peak here — the beam spot was the problem.

MIP spectra

Verdict. Physics-capable but flawed: HG chain clipping at 5 GeV, scintillator headroom short, and the module offset ~6.4 mm vertically from the MCP axis (miss fraction + capillary asymmetry: beam toward the 6/7 row, columns balanced). Actions taken → DC offsets re-set, module moved toward chs 6/7 before run 14.

Channel integrity & identification

the data format changed — re-verify before trusting anything

New array layout, verified in-data

From this run on, waveforms are stored in mV (mV = 1000·(counts/4095 − 0.5)) and the array uses slot = group·9 + channel: slots 0–7 = DT5742 ch 0–7, slot 8 = MCP copy (group 0), slots 9–16 = DT5742 ch 8–15, slot 17 = MCP copy (group 1).

Verified from the data itself: corr(slot 8, slot 17) = 0.998 — the two TR0 copies; slot 16 correlates 0.90 with LG ch 6 — its high-gain partner. DT5742-native pairing unchanged from run 12 (all four verified, r = 0.88–0.95). Post-trigger 74% puts prompt pulses at sample ~52, so baselines come from samples 0–39 (tight — 70% recommended).

2

Cherenkov coincidence: 76 / 1,000 = 7.6% electrons — consistent with run 12's 9.9% at these statistics. HG gains ~2× run 12 (bias raise, step 1); MIPs re-fitted from this run's own off-coincidence sample for the normalization below.

High-gain vs low-gain transfer (wall-aware)

The clip wall is measured per capillary from the HG amplitude spectrum (3,143–3,186 ADC-eq, top row) and the transfer line is fit only in the linear region below 0.72 × wall — shaded band, solid line = fit, dashed = extrapolation. Ratios 2.39 / 2.50 / 2.66 / 2.83 (caps 4/5/6/7), fit windows LG 30–695…815. Only 25 clipped HG pulses in the whole run needed recovery (vs 587 in run 12).

An electron peak exists now

Centering turned run 12's featureless ramp into a real response peak: mean 2992 ± 36, σ/E 33.6 ± 1.4% (position-smearing dominated; the run-12 edge bound puts the intrinsic response nearer 10%). Every energy-scan point now yields a fittable peak → linearity and width trends come directly.

The srCFD follows the collaboration code (jwwetzel/radical, reduce/Reducer.C): threshold at 15% of the LG-predicted true HG peak, guarded above noise and below the clip shelf, timed on the intact steep edge — a clipped top never matters. Width from the repo’s tebSigma robust estimator. At 5 GeV it agrees with plain CFD (clipping is rare); its advantage appears at the high-energy scan points where the HG rails. Inter-group jitter is unchanged from run 12 (104.5 ps); all numbers include the MCP contribution once, unsubtracted. The repo’s reference-free (DW−UP)/2 method needs two-ended readout — not available on this single-ended module.

Verdict. Complete and clean. Configuration frozen (bias, offsets, post-trigger, geometry) — this run is the 5 GeV anchor of the energy scan. Recommended scan: multiplicative spacing (1 · 1.5 · 2 · 3 · 4.5 · 7 · 10 GeV), 20k events per point, watch the HG rail fraction as energy rises.
